research_rationale: Executive Order 12353 of 1982-03-23 (47 FR 12785) set up the Combined Federal Campaign under the Director of the Office of Personnel Management. The held official text was read in full; its first inventory omitted sections 8 and 9, which follow the page break, so the inventory is corrected to nine sections with section 9 split into a performed revocation and a continuing savings sentence. Executive Orders 12404 and 13743 amended it and were read in full; neither ends it. The extracted U.S. Code note to 5 U.S.C. 1101 (not cited) reproduces the order as amended, the eCFR bounded search as of 2026-10-14 returned current regulations that rely on it, and the Federal Register catalog search found no revocation. The order is therefore claimed in force on 2026-10-14. The held official text is a machine text layer (OCR) of the Federal Register page; its spans quote the OCR text.
savings_reason: Both amending orders preserved rules made under the order: Executive Order 12404 section 2 and Executive Order 13743 section 2(d) say rules, regulations and directives continued or issued under Executive Order 12353 continue in effect until revoked or modified under the amending order. These rules (OPM rules at 5 CFR part 950) are independent implementing instruments that continue while the order stays in force; the order itself has no end date and no savings of its own other than the section 9 continuation of Executive Order 10927 directives.
conflict_resolutions: {"PARTIAL_END_CANDIDATE_ON_YES_ORDER":"The only candidate end is a 2007-08-28 Postal Service rule, FR Doc. E7-16986 (72 FR 49195). Its held text says references to Executive Order 10927 are obsolete because that order was revoked by Executive Order 12353 on 1982-03-23, so it describes this order as the revoking instrument and does not revoke, supersede or amend Executive Order 12353."}
earlier_end_check: Searched the held corpus for the order number: the held later instruments that act on the order are Executive Order 12404 (1983-02-10) and Executive Order 13743 (2016-10-13), both amendments, and neither revokes the order. 5 CFR 950.101, 32 CFR 228.16, 32 CFR 234.13, 18 CFR 1300.102 and several Federal Register notices cite the order as operating authority. The order has no sunset, no expiry date and no statute on which it depends. The 2007 Postal Service rule is addressed in the conflict resolution. No earlier end exists.
scope_check: Scope is the whole order: sections 1 through 9 as held in the official Federal Register text (47 FR 12785-12786, 1982-03-25). Sections 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 were amended by the two later orders; sections 4, 7 and 8 stand in their original words; section 9 holds a performed revocation and a continuing savings sentence. Amendments are later events, not ends, under the strike-and-insert ruling of 2026-10-21.
independent_command_check: The order is a set of continuing directions to the OPM Director (arrange and run the Combined Federal Campaign), not a one-time task; each direction continues while the order is in force. The only spent command is the revocation of Executive Order 10927 in section 9, recorded as its own terminated clause with its own date.
savings_check: Rules continued under the order survive amendment by explicit provisions in Executive Order 12404 section 2 and Executive Order 13743 section 2(d); the order has no end to trigger savings. The savings state is continuing_independent.
